content:
The image shows a corn ear that has been split open, revealing:
- Massive black powdery/sooty mass replacing the kernels entirely
- White fibrous strands (vascular tissue) visible beneath the black spore mass
- The husk is dried and pale/tan
- The black material is dusty and friable — classic teliospore mass

This is clearly **Common_smut** — the characteristic massive black gall filled with dark teliospores on corn ear tissue. Head_smut also produces black spores but typically affects the tassel/head rather than the ear, and looks different in structure. This image shows the ear being completely converted to a dark spore mass, which is the hallmark of *Ustilago maydis* (Common smut).

This is distinct from Head_smut (which affects tassels) and Ear_rots (which show mold rather than dry black spore masses)."}
